title: I built a no-code lab where you describe a strategy in plain English, an AI builds it, and it stress-tests whether it's actually real
author: Scoop_11
selftext:
I've been deep in the "AI builds your trading strategy" space and kept hitting two problems, so I built something to fix them for myself.

1) AI makes it trivial to generate a beautiful backtest — which means a beautiful backtest barely proves anything anymore. I wanted the AI to build the strategy AND immediately tell me whether it's robust or just curve-fit.

2) I'd end up with a few decent strategies and no clean way to combine them into one portfolio and see how the blend actually behaves.

So I made this site where:

\- Describe a strategy in plain English (or build it from visual blocks) and an AI turns it into a real, runnable strategy — no code.

\- It backtests on real S&P 500 data and runs walk-forward, Monte-Carlo and a deflated-Sharpe check, so you find out fast whether the curve survives out-of-sample or falls apart.

\- Then you can combine several strategies into one portfolio with money-weighted returns.

It's in open beta, so everything's free right now — no card, nothing to buy.

[app.quantheonlab.com](http://app.quantheonlab.com)

It's early and rough in places. Curious how this community thinks about it: when an AI can spin up infinite strategies, what's your filter for telling a real edge from an overfit one?

Thanks :)

comments.author: brt100
comments.body: Tried it but was maxed out @ 2000 characters in 'Describe'

replies.author: Scoop_11
replies.body:
Thanks for actually trying it — and good catch. The "Describe" box is capped at 2000 chars right now; it's tuned for a concise plain-English description (usually a sentence or two), so I set it lower than it needs to be.

Two things that probably help: if you were pasting something bigger — a full spec or code from another platform — the "Paste code" tab in the same dialog takes \~10x more (and even turns indicators it doesn't know into reusable blocks). And there's a "Modify" mode to layer changes on one at a time instead of one giant prompt.

Either way, 2000 is tighter than it should be for Describe — I'm bumping it. Appreciate the report 🙏

comments.author: tinfoil_powers
comments.body: I'm doing the same but my AI agent building out a full-on data flow instead of just writing some code. That way I can plug and play my strategy bits and bobs like Lego bricks, or it can.

replies.author: Scoop_11
replies.body:
Nice — that's basically the same bet I made. Under the hood everything compiles to a visual node graph, so a strategy literally is Lego bricks you snap together — or the AI snaps them for you from a plain-English description. Reusable bits get saved too: any indicator the AI mints becomes a "brick" in your palette you can drop into other strategies.

Curious how you're handling the data-flow graph on your side — fully agent-built, or human-in-the-loop where you rearrange the bricks after? Always good to see someone chasing the same plug-and-play idea.
